title: Imaging Topotactic Phase Transitions in Freestanding SrCoO3-x Membranes
content: Strontium cobaltite (SrCoO3-x, SCO) is known for multiple electronic and magnetic ground states which can be tuned through topotactic phase transitions (TPTs), i.e., structural transformations involving the insertion or removal of oxygen ions in the crystal lattice. Its relatively low oxygen vacancy formation energy and high oxygen vacancy conductivity [1, 2] place SCO on the verge of a structural transition such that an external stimulus can readily trigger the TPT between the ferromagnetic (FM) perovskite (P) SrCoO3 and antiferromagnetic (AFM) brownmillerite (BM) SrCoO2.5 phases [3, 4]. A distinctive characteristic of the SrCoO2.5 phase is its alternating sublayers of tetrahedrally- and octahedrally-coordinated CoO4 and CoO6 polyhedra stacked along the [001] direction, resulting in 1-dimensional oxygen vacancy channels (OVCs) along the [110]-type direction [5, 6] (Figure 1a). Understanding the local domain structure as this TPT takes place is of great interest for functional oxide research ranging from new electromagnetic ground states in reduced crystal structures to energy-efficient resistive switching devices for neuromorphic computing [7, 8].
